How do you determine whether a specific: BNB Accelerator uses a layered review: one team member checks the relevant city or county and any HOA, a second team member reconfirms the findings, and the property is checked again under contract. The review also considers septic capacity and permitted bedroom count where relevant.

Confirm the exact address, intended stay length, permit eligibility and any ownership-transfer requirements. Verbal confirmation is part of the process, but keep the applicable ordinances, recorded restrictions and written responses where available. An existing rental listing does not establish your right to operate.
Who checks city, county and HOA short-te: The team performs a preliminary review, a second team member checks the findings, and the property is reviewed again under contract. Ask for the underlying rules and the specific address-level conclusions so your agent or attorney can resolve any ambiguity before your contingency deadlines.
What does it mean if an STR is grandfath: An existing use may be allowed to continue after a rule changes, subject to the jurisdiction's conditions. Grandfathered status may depend on continuous operation, permit renewal, ownership or other facts and may not survive a sale. BNB Accelerator generally avoids sourcing properties that depend on uncertain exceptions.
What happens if a property is legal toda: Future rule changes can restrict or end rental use, impose new conditions or allow some existing operators to continue. The outcome depends on the adopted rule and any applicable legal protections. Do not assume grandfathered status will protect the property. Evaluate a fallback use and the financial effect of losing STR permission before buying.
How should I think about regulatory risk: BNB Accelerator considers regulatory risk in tiers. Purpose-built STR communities with explicit governing documents may offer a clearer operating path than mixed residential communities. Markets with recent rule changes or ambiguous restrictions need closer review.

These are screening categories, not legal guarantees. Review municipal and county rules as well as HOA documents, permit conditions and address-specific restrictions. Local economic reliance on tourism does not prevent future rule changes.
Does being in an STR-compliant neighborh: No. Confirm the exact address, zoning, permit availability, occupancy limits, septic capacity and any recorded or HOA restrictions. The team checks the individual property rather than relying only on a neighborhood's reputation.
What are the major deadlines between con: The major milestones are the earnest-money deposit, inspection and due diligence, financing or loan commitment, appraisal protection and closing. Timing comes from your signed contract and any amendments; there is no universal deposit or inspection period.

Your agent and transaction coordinator should record each date, notice requirement and consequence. A missed closing date may trigger default or other remedies under the agreement. Extensions require the approvals and signatures specified by the contract.
What do I need to do vs. what does the B: The team coordinates communication with your agent, lender, title company and other transaction participants. It helps track earnest money, arrange inspections and specialist reviews, review repair negotiations, coordinate insurance quotes and appraisal milestones, arrange signing, introduce managers and designers, and review closing figures.

You approve decisions and costs, send your funds, provide lender and title documentation, sign agreements and amendments, and choose your manager and designer. Ask the lead transaction coordinator when any responsibility is unclear.

Deadline tracking does not guarantee a deposit refund. Your agent or attorney must confirm the available contractual rights and proper notices, and any extension depends on the required parties agreeing.
When do inspection, appraisal, insurance: Title work begins after the contract is accepted. Inspection and specialist reviews must fit the contract's due-diligence deadlines. The lender orders the appraisal on a schedule that supports financing and closing.

Start insurance quotes early enough to identify coverage or affordability problems, then confirm the final binder before funding. Some tasks run in parallel; your transaction coordinator will map the schedule for the property.
Do I need to attend closing?: You usually do not need to attend the title office. A mobile notary or another lender- and title-approved signing process may be available. Confirm identification, location and scheduling requirements early.

If you will be outside the United States, notify the team before committing to the closing date. Title and your lender must approve any overseas signing, remote process or power of attorney; availability varies.
What happens if I’m travelling or unavai: Tell your transaction coordinator where you will be and when you can sign. A mobile notary may accommodate domestic travel. Overseas signing or a power of attorney requires advance lender and title approval.
If an approved signing method cannot be arranged, request a written closing extension through your agent. Do not assume the seller must agree or that travel automatically excuses a missed deadline.
When is my EMD actually at risk?: Your earnest-money deposit can be at risk if you default, waive a protection, miss a required deadline or terminate without a contractual right. The signed agreement and applicable law determine the outcome.

Track notice requirements as well as dates. A contingency does not protect you automatically if you fail to exercise it properly. Ask your agent or attorney to confirm your rights before a deadline passes.
What contingencies protect my EMD?: Inspection, financing, appraisal and other negotiated contingencies may provide termination rights, subject to their conditions, deadlines and notice requirements. Protections vary by contract and may have been limited or waived.
Review the actual clauses with your agent or attorney. A concern about the property does not by itself establish a right to cancel or receive your deposit back.
What happens if an inspection issue isn’: Contact your agent and transaction coordinator before the deadline. Options may include a signed extension, an agreed repair amendment or timely termination if your contract permits it.

A protective termination is still a real contractual notice. Use it only on your agent's or attorney's advice, with your authorization and proper delivery. Continued negotiations do not automatically revive a terminated agreement.
Can I get my EMD back if the appraisal i: Possibly, if your signed appraisal contingency applies and you exercise it correctly before its deadline. First consider whether a lower price or another acceptable arrangement can be negotiated.
An appraisal gap provision, waived contingency or missed notice can change your rights. Title may need a signed release or another authorized resolution before returning funds.
What happens if I walk away?: Before terminating, have your agent or attorney confirm the contractual basis, deadline and required notice. If a valid contingency permits cancellation, follow the specified process and obtain the deposit release.
Title may need both parties' release or a legally authorized resolution. Walking away outside your contractual rights can put your deposit at risk and create additional liability.
Seller repair vs. seller credit , which: A lender-approved credit or price reduction can give you control over the repair after closing. Seller-completed repairs may be necessary for safety, financing, insurance or rental readiness.

Compare repair quality, timing, available cash and lender limits. If the seller performs work, document the required scope, permits and completion evidence, and arrange a reinspection where appropriate.
Does the inspector provide repair estima: A standard home inspection primarily identifies condition issues and may not include reliable repair pricing. Ask the inspector what is included, then obtain written quotes from appropriately qualified contractors or specialists for material issues.
Should appraisal happen before or after: Coordinate both with your lender and transaction coordinator. Reviewing inspection findings first may avoid paying for an appraisal on a property you decide to reject, but waiting too long can delay closing. The lender's requirements and contract deadlines control the schedule.
What happens if it comes in below purcha: Review the report with the lender and agent, then consider a price reduction, supported reconsideration of value, additional buyer cash or termination if the contract permits it. Update the pro forma before deciding. The seller is not required to match the appraisal.
What happens if it comes in above the pu: The appraisal may support a value above your agreed price, but it is an opinion at a point in time. It does not guarantee resale proceeds, immediately available equity or a larger purchase loan. Confirm the lender's valuation and loan-to-value rules.
Why is STR insurance different from home: Ordinary homeowners or long-term landlord coverage may exclude or limit paying-guest activity. Obtain a policy or endorsement that expressly covers the intended short-term rental use. Ask a licensed insurance professional to confirm coverage for your property, guest activity and amenities.
What coverage should an STR policy inclu: Discuss replacement-cost dwelling coverage, furnishings, liability, loss of rental income, deductibles and exclusions with a licensed insurance professional. Confirm pools, hot tubs and other amenities, and any flood, wind or wildfire needs.

A $1 million liability limit is a useful discussion point from our planning checklist, not a universal requirement or assurance of adequate coverage. The lender, exposure and insurer determine the appropriate policy.
How do I safely verify wire instructions: Call the title company using a telephone number you independently verified earlier in the transaction. Confirm the receiving bank, account details, payee and amount before sending funds.
A secure portal can help, but do not rely only on an emailed link or a last-minute change. If instructions change, stop and verify directly with title through the known contact.
Do I physically need to attend closing?: Often you can sign through a mobile notary or another process approved by title and your lender. Confirm the permitted location, identity documents and appointment before closing. Overseas signing or a power of attorney requires advance approval.
What does the title company do?: The title company examines ownership records, identifies liens and title exceptions, coordinates required closing documents and handles escrow or settlement where that is part of its role. Existing loans or liens may be paid off at closing rather than the property already being free of them.
Review the title commitment, exceptions and proposed policy with your agent or attorney. Roles and closing procedures vary by state.
What documents should I expect to receiv: Before closing, expect the title commitment, verified wire instructions, draft settlement figures, seller disclosures, HOA documents where applicable, inspection reports, insurance binder and agreed amendments.

Your lender supplies the applicable loan documents, appraisal and approval conditions. For covered consumer mortgages, the Closing Disclosure is generally due at least three business days before consummation. Business-purpose loans, including many DSCR loans, may be exempt and use different disclosures.

At closing, review the final settlement statement, loan documents if financed, deed, affidavits and entity documents where relevant. After closing, retain the executed package, recorded deed, title policy and loan-servicing information. Delivery timing varies.
What is the difference between the Closi: The Closing Disclosure is the standardized loan and cost disclosure used for covered consumer mortgages, generally received at least three business days before consummation. Many business-purpose loans are exempt, so confirm which disclosure applies.

The ALTA settlement statement shows transaction charges, credits, prorations and disbursements and may also be used in cash transactions. The closing package contains the documents actually signed, including the deed and any applicable note, security instrument, affidavits and disclosures.
See CFPB Closing Disclosure guidance and exempt transactions.
If I paid insurance or another expense o: Provide the receipt and proof of payment to title, the lender and transaction coordinator before final figures are approved. Confirm whether the closing line is a premium, escrow deposit or another charge.
If a duplicate payment is confirmed, ask the collecting party to correct the statement or arrange the appropriate refund. Do not assume every insurance-related line is a duplicate.
Will I ever receive unused seller credit: Do not expect unused financing concessions to become a cash payment. Seller credits must satisfy the lender's eligible-cost rules, program caps and actual-cost limits.
Review usable costs before closing. A lender-approved rate buydown or a separately negotiated price reduction may be options; neither is automatic. Fannie Mae seller-credit rules
What happens to seller credits that exce: Unused credits may be lost unless the parties and lender approve a permissible adjustment before closing. Discuss an eligible rate buydown or a negotiated purchase-price reduction early; the seller need not agree and the lender must approve the revised structure.
Credits cannot simply be redirected to furniture, renovations or cash back. Fannie Mae seller-credit rules
When do utilities transfer?: Arrange utility accounts before closing with an effective date matching the agreed possession date, commonly closing or immediately afterward. Confirm the timing with title and the seller to avoid interruption, and use the transaction coordinator's setup guide.
When can contractors/designers enter?: Once ownership and possession have transferred, arrange access through the owner or manager. Respect any existing guest stays, seller possession agreement and contractor requirements. Pre-close access needs the seller's authorization.
When do permitting and STR licensing beg: Check eligibility and required steps before going under contract. Some applications need proof of ownership and therefore begin at or after closing; others can be started earlier. Follow the local authority's process and obtain required approvals before accepting guests.
When can renovations start?: After ownership and possession transfer, required permits and approvals are in place, and access is compatible with any existing reservations. Confirm contractor licensing, insurance and the scope before work begins.
What is the full path from closing to go: The path usually includes access and utility transfers, repairs and permitted improvements, furnishing and design, inspections or licenses, photography, listing setup and management handoff.

BNB Accelerator's planning range in this client FAQ is typically 60 to 90 days after closing when meaningful work is required. A rental-ready property can launch sooner, while major construction, permits or vendor delays can take longer. Use a property-specific schedule rather than treating the range as a guarantee.
What happens if utilities cannot be tran: Contact the utility provider, transaction coordinator and title company promptly to confirm the missing document or setup step. If temporary seller service is needed, request a written arrangement defining payment and the end date. Other options may be available from the provider. Avoid operating with interrupted essential services.
Can seller credits be used to pay design: Do not assume they can. Ordinary furnishing, renovation and property-management invoices are generally outside standard financing concessions. A lender may permit specific documented expenses or an approved program structure.

Have the transaction coordinator obtain lender and title confirmation before promising a vendor payment through closing. Paying an invoice through title does not itself make the cost eligible for a seller credit.
What happens to existing Airbnb/VRBO res: Agree on a written handoff before closing: identify future stays, guest payments, deposits, operating responsibility and who communicates with guests. Account for bookings in the contract and settlement arrangements.
Airbnb does not transfer reservations to a different host account. For Vrbo, follow its current sale and host-transition process. Airbnb policy; Vrbo guidance.
Do I have to honor the seller's future r: That depends on applicable law, your purchase agreement, reservation terms and the approved operating transition. Have your agent or attorney review the obligations before signing. Do not assume a property sale automatically cancels guest commitments or transfers them to you.
Can existing reservations be transferred: Airbnb reservations cannot move to a new host account. Vrbo has a property-sale and host-transition policy; confirm the required process with its support team before relying on a booking handoff.
Use a documented, platform-compliant plan for guest communication and operating responsibility. Airbnb policy; Vrbo transition guidance.
If reservations are cancelled, can that: Cancellations can affect guests and may create contractual or platform consequences. Responsibility depends on the account, agreements and circumstances. Review the platform's current rules and agree who handles refunds, guest communications and any costs before closing.
Does the seller's Airbnb/VRBO listing tr: Do not treat the property purchase as a listing or account transfer. Airbnb account ownership cannot transfer to a different host. Confirm Vrbo's current property-sale process directly with support, including any treatment of listing information and reviews.
Document rights to photos and other marketing assets separately. Airbnb policy; Vrbo guidance.
What information should I request from t: Request booking and payout reports, occupancy and nightly rates, cancellations, refunds, management statements, operating expenses and lodging-tax records. Ask for future reservations and amounts already collected.
Separate owner use from guest stays and reconcile reported income with supporting records. Also verify permits, furnishing inventory, maintenance history and the proposed transition plan.
When should my new property manager take: Set an explicit handoff date and responsibilities before closing. Confirm account permissions, guest communication, payout routing, cleaning schedules, existing reservations and launch readiness.
Ownership does not automatically change the platform account or management contract. The seller, new manager and you should coordinate any required platform-approved transition.
